questions.question: In the process of cell division, the formation of phragmoplast between the two daughter nuclei occurs during:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cytokinesis**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cytokinesis** is the process during cell division where the **cytoplasm of a parental cell is divided between two daughter cells**.
 
• The formation of the **phragmoplast** occurs during cytokinesis in plant cells.
 
• The phragmoplast is a structure that serves as a **scaffold for cell plate assembly** and subsequent formation of a new cell wall separating the two daughter cells.
 
• It is essential for the successful completion of cell division in plants, ensuring that each daughter cell receives the necessary cellular components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell division** consists of two main processes: mitosis (karyokinesis) and cytokinesis.
 
• **Mitosis** is the division of the nucleus, whereas **cytokinesis** is the division of the cytoplasm.
 
• In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs through the formation of a cleavage furrow that pinches the cell into two.
 
• In plant cells, the **phragmoplast** guides the formation of a cell plate, which eventually develops into a separating cell wall.
 
• The **G0 phase** is a resting phase where the cell is not actively preparing to divide.
 
• The **S phase** is the part of the cell cycle where DNA replication occurs.

questions.question: A tunnel that runs through the cell wall between two plant cells is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasmodesmata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plasmodesmata** are microscopic channels that traverse the cell walls of plant cells, establishing a direct connection between the cytoplasm of adjacent cells.
 
• They facilitate **intercellular communication** and the exchange of nutrients, ions, signaling molecules, and other substances.
 
• Plasmodesmata play a critical role in maintaining the **symplastic pathway**, allowing transport of materials through the cytoplasm.
 
• They are formed during **cell division** and remain as permanent structures, enabling plants to function as a cohesive system.
 
• Their structure includes a central **desmotubule** derived from the endoplasmic reticulum, surrounded by cytoplasmic sleeves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Wall**:

 
 
• It is a rigid, protective layer made of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin in plants.
 
• It provides structural support, protection, and regulates cell growth.
 
 
 
• **Symplastic Pathway**:
 
 
• The route of transport of water and solutes through the cytoplasm of cells interconnected by plasmodesmata.
 
• This pathway is crucial for the efficient sharing of resources and signaling across plant tissues.
 
 
 
• **Apoplastic Pathway**:
 
 
• Transport occurs through the cell wall and intercellular spaces without crossing membranes.
 
• It is complementary to the symplastic pathway and is important for water and solute movement.
 
 
 
• **Desmotubule**:
 
 
• A tube-like structure within the plasmodesmata, derived from the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (ER).
 
• It helps in maintaining the structure and selective transport of materials between cells.
 
 
 
• **Peroxisomes**:
 
 
• Small organelles found in cells that contain enzymes for metabolic processes, such as breaking down fatty acids and detoxifying hydrogen peroxide.
 
• They are not related to plasmodesmata but are crucial for cellular metabolism.

questions.question: When a cell divides by meiosis it produces ______ new cells.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 4.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meiosis** is a manner wherein a single cell divides two times to produce four cells containing half the original amount of genetic statistics. 
 
• The chromosome pairs line up subsequent to every difference along the middle (equator) of the mobile.
 
• Meiosis produces** 4 haploid cells. ** Mitosis produces **2 diploid cells. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The motive of meiosis **is to supply gametes or intercourse cells.
 
• **Meiosis** takes place within the testes and ovaries of men and women, respectively, inside the primordial germ cells.
 
• **The manner **of meiosis become first defined in the **mid-1870s by Oscar Hertwig.**

questions.question: The cells having well - organized nucleus with a nuclear membrane are designated as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**eukaryotic cells.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Eukaryotic cells are characterized by a well-organized nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane.
 
• This is where the cell's DNA is stored.
 
• These cells are generally larger and more complex than prokaryotic cells.
 
• Eukaryotic cells have various types of organelles, including mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi apparatus, which are enclosed by membranes and have specific functions.
 
• Eukaryotic cells can be found in a wide variety of organisms, including plants, animals, and fungi.
 
• The complex structure of eukaryotic cells allows for compartmentalization and specialization of functions, which enables these cells to perform more complex tasks than prokaryotic cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The transportation mechanism in cells by which food or other useful molecules from the outside are carried inside the cell is known as ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Endocytosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Endocytosis** is a cellular process in which substances are brought into the cell.
 
• It involves the cell membrane folding around the desired molecules to form a vesicle that is brought into the cell.
 
• Endocytosis is crucial for the intake of nutrients and other essential molecules that cannot pass through the cell membrane by diffusion.
 
• There are different types of endocytosis, including phagocytosis (ingestion of large particles) and pinocytosis (ingestion of fluids and small molecules).
 
• Endocytosis plays a significant role in cellular signaling, nutrient uptake, and immune responses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exocytosis** is the process by which cells expel materials in vesicles by fusing them with the cell membrane.
 
• **Osmosis** refers to the movement of water molecules through a semi-permeable membrane from a region of low solute concentration to high solute concentration.
 
• **Diffusion** is the passive movement of particles from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration.
 
• **Phagocytosis** is a type of endocytosis where the cell engulfs large particles or even whole cells, typically seen in immune cells like macrophages.
 
• **Pinocytosis** is another type of endocytosis where the cell engulfs extracellular fluid and dissolved solutes, often referred to as "cell drinking."
